          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable.           "excerpt": "def test_records_are_schema_validated_and_atomic(state: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an invalid or partial record becomes visible, or concurrent updates overwrite each other\n    (criterion 19).\"\"\"\n    job_id = jobs.new_job_id()\n    path = record_path(job_id)\n    good = jobs.new_record(job_id, [\"echo\", \"hi\"], \"/work\", str(state / f\"{job_id}.log\"))\n    for broken in (\n        {**good, \"schema\": True},\n        {**good, \"schema\": 1.0},\n        {**good, \"state\": \"sleeping\"},\n        {**good, \"command\": []},\n        {**good, \"groups\": [{\"pgid\": \"x\", \"pid\": 1, \"start\": None}]},\n        {k: v for k, v in good.items() if k != \"log\"},\n        {**good, \"extra\": 1},\n    ):\n        with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n            jobs.write_record(path, broken)\n        assert not path.exists(), \"an invalid record was published\"\n    jobs.write_record(path, good)\n    before = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    real_fsync = os.fsync\n\n    def failing_fsync(_fd: int) -> None:\n        raise OSError(\"disk\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", failing_fsync)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError, match=\"disk\"):\n        jobs.write_record(path, {**good, \"state\": \"running\"})\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", real_fsync)\n    assert path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == before, \"a failed write left a partial record\"\n    assert sorted(p.name for p in state.iterdir()) == [path.name]  # no temporary file remains\n    path.write_text(before[: len(before) // 2], encoding=\"utf-8\")  # a truncated record is refused, never repaired\n    with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n        jobs.read_record(path)\n    path.write_text(before, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    def add(n: int):\n        return lambda record: record[\"groups\"].append({\"pgid\": n, \"pid\": n, \"start\": None})\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=jobs.update_record, args=(path, add(n))) for n in range(1, 9)]\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.start()\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.join()\n    assert sorted(g[\"pgid\"] for g in jobs.read_record(path)[\"groups\"]) == list(range(1, 9))\n",

          "excerpt": "REPAIR_ANSWER = (\n    \"Answer with one fixed line per taken row: `<ID>: fixed — tests/<path>::<function>`,\\n\"\n    \"`<ID>: fixed — guard test — tests/<path>::<function>` or `<ID>: fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\\n\"\n    \"Headings, fences and report prose around the fixed lines are\\n\"\n    \"ignored, but a colon line whose id looks like a finding id (`L1-2`, `F-12`) and names no taken row\\n\"\n    \"still fails. Letters-hyphen-digits ids count only for prefixes used by this change's row ids;\\n\"\n    \"`L<digits>-<digits>` always counts; the prefix `L` counts only when the change has a loop row.\\n\"\n    \"A colon line whose right side is a fixed status (`fixed — …`) also fails when its id names no\\n\"\n    \"taken row, whatever the id's shape. A taken row takes exactly one distinct fixed line: a repeated\\n\"\n    \"identical line counts once, and two different fixed lines for one row fail the attempt, so give\\n\"\n    \"each row's status once and leave the rest of the report as prose. Write a `|` inside a reason as `\\\\|`.\\n\"\n    \"An ordinary code row needs a test that fails on the baseline's code, which the runner runs; a row\\n\"\n    \"taken as `taken — guard test — <reason>` is answered with the guard form instead, and the runner\\n\"\n    \"requires a nonempty unquoted reason (a quoted or backticked reason is not authorisation) and\\n\"\n    \"proves its named test twice on the attempt's code - qualifying red with `STAGE2_PLANT_FAULT=1`,\\n\"\n    \"whose fault the test itself plants, then clean green without the switch; the planting branch stays\\n\"\n    \"in the kept test so the proof can be repeated. Only a row taken as\\n\"\n    f\"`taken — not a test — <reason>` may be answered `not a test`. {RAISING_FAULT_SENTENCE} Do not edit `findings.md`; findings.md is the runner's audit file, and an\\n\"\n    \"edit of it is restored before the checks, so the edit alone never fails the attempt. After every\\n\"\n    \"attempt the runner also restores `status` and `implementation_status` in the change's `spec.md`,\\n\"\n    \"optional `design.md` and `plan.md` to the values they had before the call, so never edit those\\n\"\n    \"fields; a repair whose remedy needs a lifecycle change is repaired by hand, not by an attempt.\\n\"\n    \"A hand repair\\n\"\n    \"is booked in the row's own Status as\\n\"\n    \"one of the three fixed statuses above; a Status that still begins `taken` while naming a fix\\n\"\n    \"(`; fixed by …`, `; fixed: …`, `; repaired by …`) refuses the repair before any call.\\n\"\n    \"Backtick-quoted markers do not count; an unquoted marker beside a backtick span still refuses the repair.\\n\"\n    \"The runner keeps every attempt's complete answer as protected local evidence and names the file in\\n\"\n    \"the attempt's diagnostics, where a rejected answer can be read again.\"\n)\n",

    "The ADR draft's Validation section claims that unit and concurrency tests confirm atomic locked reads/writes of loop/lane/job JSON state, deterministic Markdown rendering round-trips, and \"zero control-flow regex reads of rendered tables\".     "The premise that loop state is Markdown parsed back is only partly true today: the run's stage snapshot is already a JSON object carried on one `Loop state:` line and parsed with json.loads in read_state, so part of the state surface is structured and merely embedded in Markdown.",
    "Quote-fragility in the release path is already covered, not uncovered: test_a_quoted_release_heading_or_no_loop_line_moves_no_release and test_the_state_line_below_a_quoting_cell_is_still_read pin that a quoted heading or a quoting table cell cannot stand in for the runner's own line or hide the state line, which weakens the case that only structured state can prevent that class of bug.",
    "House rule 9 and house rule 11 say a rule of this kind takes hold through a check that goes red, not through prose, but every loop-record check I read reads loop.md itself, so the checks move with the format rather than holding a boundary that survives it.",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_round_and_its_consumed_stage_land_in_one_write(world: World, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"R-6 of the review-swarm review: no window between the round and the consumption.\"\"\"\n    world.write_findings(VERDICT)\n    world.script(pi=[{\"model\": model, \"stdout\": rows(1)} for model in TEST_FREE])\n    writes: list[str] = []\n    original = Path.write_text\n\n    def counting(self, data, *args, **kwargs):\n        writes.append(self.name)\n        return original(self, data, *args, **kwargs)\n\n    replaced: list[str] = []\n    real_replace = stage2.replace_record\n\n    def replacing(path, text):\n        replaced.append(Path(path).name)\n        return real_replace(path, text)\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, \"write_text\", counting)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"replace_record\", replacing)\n    assert world.run(\"review-loop\") == 0\n    record = world.record().read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    monkeypatch.undo()\n    # One write reaches loop.md, and it replaces the file whole: the fresh run's snapshot line and the\n    # round that carries its own consumption land together (DL-A-4 of the deep review).\n    assert writes.count(\"loop.md\") == 0 and replaced == [\"loop.md\"], (writes, replaced)\n    assert '\"consumed\": [\"free\"]' in record.replace(\" \", \" \"), record[-400:]\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_records_are_schema_validated_and_atomic(state: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an invalid or partial record becomes visible, or concurrent updates overwrite each other\n    (criterion 19).\"\"\"\n    job_id = jobs.new_job_id()\n    path = record_path(job_id)\n    good = jobs.new_record(job_id, [\"echo\", \"hi\"], \"/work\", str(state / f\"{job_id}.log\"))\n    for broken in (\n        {**good, \"schema\": True},\n        {**good, \"schema\": 1.0},\n        {**good, \"state\": \"sleeping\"},\n        {**good, \"command\": []},\n        {**good, \"groups\": [{\"pgid\": \"x\", \"pid\": 1, \"start\": None}]},\n        {k: v for k, v in good.items() if k != \"log\"},\n        {**good, \"extra\": 1},\n    ):\n        with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n            jobs.write_record(path, broken)\n        assert not path.exists(), \"an invalid record was published\"\n    jobs.write_record(path, good)\n    before = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    real_fsync = os.fsync\n\n    def failing_fsync(_fd: int) -> None:\n        raise OSError(\"disk\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", failing_fsync)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError, match=\"disk\"):\n        jobs.write_record(path, {**good, \"state\": \"running\"})\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", real_fsync)\n    assert path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == before, \"a failed write left a partial record\"\n    assert sorted(p.name for p in state.iterdir()) == [path.name]  # no temporary file remains\n    path.write_text(before[: len(before) // 2], encoding=\"utf-8\")  # a truncated record is refused, never repaired\n    with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n        jobs.read_record(path)\n    path.write_text(before, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    def add(n: int):\n        return lambda record: record[\"groups\"].append({\"pgid\": n, \"pid\": n, \"start\": None})\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=jobs.update_record, args=(path, add(n))) for n in range(1, 9)]\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.start()\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.join()\n    assert sorted(g[\"pgid\"] for g in jobs.read_record(path)[\"groups\"]) == list(range(1, 9))\n",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_supersession(change: str, root: Path) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Serialize release and supersession across this repository's worktrees.\"\"\"\n    common = os.fsdecode(run_git(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--git-common-dir\").stdout).strip()\n    common_path = (root / common).resolve()\n    digest = hashlib.sha256(str(common_path).encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()[:16]\n    path = record_base() / f\"supersession-{digest}-{change}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            holder = handle.read().strip() or \"unknown worktree\"\n            raise Refused(f\"supersession lock for {change} is held by {holder}; nothing is changed\") from error\n        try:\n            handle.seek(0)\n            handle.truncate()\n            handle.write(record_key(change, root))\n            handle.flush()\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish `text` at `path` whole or not at all (same-directory temporary file, then rename).\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(text)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "end_line": 237,
          "excerpt": "def run(root: Path, rev_arg: str | None, out: Callable[[str], object] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"One report: table to stdout, JSON Lines to the state file, the path printed last.\"\"\"\n    if out is None:\n        out = sys.stdout.write  # looked up at call time, so a redirected stdout is honoured\n    sha = full_commit(root, rev_arg or \"HEAD\")\n    findings, gaps, outside = collect(root, sha)\n    models = totals_of(findings)\n    complete = not gaps\n    target = state_root() / output_relative(root, rev_arg, sha)\n    records = jsonl_records(sha, complete, models, findings, gaps)\n    body = \"\".join(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\" for record in records)\n    try:\n        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        target.write_text(body, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except OSError as exc:\n        gaps.append(reader.Gap(str(target), None, f\"cannot write report: {exc}\"))\n        complete = False\n        records = jsonl_records(sha, complete, models, findings, gaps)\n\n    out(f\"Findings per model — cutoff commit {sha}\\n\\n\")\n    out(table(models, records) + \"\\n\")\n    if gaps:\n        out(f\"\\nIncomplete — {len(gaps)} gap(s), the counts above are not complete:\\n\")\n        for gap in gaps:\n            name = gap.id or \"(input)\"\n            out(f\"- {gap.path}: {name}: {gap.reason}\\n\")\n    if outside:\n        out(\"\\nOutside the count:\\n\")\n        for entry in outside:\n            out(f\"- {entry.change}: {entry.path}: {entry.label} (line {entry.line}): {entry.rows} row(s)\\n\")\n    out(f\"{target}\\n\")\n    return 0 if complete else 1\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The review loop (phase 4b)",
          "end_line": 1964,
          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills.   "counter_evidence": [
    "The newest subsystem does not follow the draft ADR's own separation: `scripts/stage2_research_run.py::compose` renders the run manifest, the source map, the history and every seat report as fenced `research-swarm/v2` JSON blocks inside research.md, beside the sealed store — so an existing, working producer keeps machine records in Markdown, and plans/changes/state-first-records/research.md of this very change carries such manifest blocks.",
    "Release is not a pure reader of one source either: `scripts/stage2.py::_release_locked` reconciles an already-appended block by comparing `released_digest(text)`, `record_digest(record)` and `matches_released_identity`, whose docstring admits older blocks hashed Origin — a compatibility ladder that a JSON-only record would have to reproduce or retire deliberately.",
    "Not every stop is derived from state: `scripts/stage2.py::release_loop` refuses a release unless a `Phase 6 verdict:` line stands in findings.md after the last release or restart, so the verdict itself is prose a human reviewer wrote, not a record field.",
    "The availability receipt is a second, single-use state object with its own lifetime: `scripts/stage2_availability.py::consume` invalidates it on a binding mismatch or an age beyond `max_age_seconds`, and `spend` deletes it only after the first round is written, so a resumed run after a crash mid-round may or may not still hold its receipt — I did not read `binding()` to say which."
  ],

The lines after the\n    note, up to the next round heading, are the reviewer's; every other line is the record's own. A line\n    of the reviewer is quoted when written, so it cannot become a round heading.\n    \"\"\"\n    lines = []\n    reviewer = False\n    for line in record.splitlines():\n        if ROUND_HEADING.match(line):\n            reviewer = False\n        elif reviewer and FROM_LINE.fullmatch(line):\n            # Every reviewer line is quoted, so an unquoted `From <member>:` is the runner's: it closes one\n            # member's words and names the next member's (DL-B-3).\n            reviewer = False\n        elif not reviewer and line.strip() == NOT_ROWS_NOTE:\n            lines.append((line, False))\n            reviewer = True\n            continue\n        lines.append((line, reviewer))\n    return lines\n",

          "excerpt": "def record_rows(record: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"The loop rows of the record: every table line of its own whose first cell is a loop id.\n\n    Only the record's own lines are read, never the reviewer's words, which are carried as they came: a\n    table line the reviewer wrote is not a row the orchestrator has to decide, whatever its first cell says.\n\n    Nine cells are known.           "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills. The prompt carries the implementation diff up to\nthe shared bound of `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (4000 lines); a cut, whether by\nthat bound or by the free stage's own file or total limits, is recorded in the\nround, and a round over a cut diff never counts as clean (R-12, R-15). When\nevery free member fails with a rate-limit (429) or unavailability error, ",

          "excerpt": "def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish `text` at `path` whole or not at all (same-directory temporary file, then rename).\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(text)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_records_are_schema_validated_and_atomic(state: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an invalid or partial record becomes visible, or concurrent updates overwrite each other\n    (criterion 19).\"\"\"\n    job_id = jobs.new_job_id()\n    path = record_path(job_id)\n    good = jobs.new_record(job_id, [\"echo\", \"hi\"], \"/work\", str(state / f\"{job_id}.log\"))\n    for broken in (\n        {**good, \"schema\": True},\n        {**good, \"schema\": 1.0},\n        {**good, \"state\": \"sleeping\"},\n        {**good, \"command\": []},\n        {**good, \"groups\": [{\"pgid\": \"x\", \"pid\": 1, \"start\": None}]},\n        {k: v for k, v in good.items() if k != \"log\"},\n        {**good, \"extra\": 1},\n    ):\n        with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n            jobs.write_record(path, broken)\n        assert not path.exists(), \"an invalid record was published\"\n    jobs.write_record(path, good)\n    before = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    real_fsync = os.fsync\n\n    def failing_fsync(_fd: int) -> None:\n        raise OSError(\"disk\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", failing_fsync)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError, match=\"disk\"):\n        jobs.write_record(path, {**good, \"state\": \"running\"})\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", real_fsync)\n    assert path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == before, \"a failed write left a partial record\"\n    assert sorted(p.name for p in state.iterdir()) == [path.name]  # no temporary file remains\n    path.write_text(before[: len(before) // 2], encoding=\"utf-8\")  # a truncated record is refused, never repaired\n    with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n        jobs.read_record(path)\n    path.write_text(before, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    def add(n: int):\n        return lambda record: record[\"groups\"].append({\"pgid\": n, \"pid\": n, \"start\": None})\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=jobs.update_record, args=(path, add(n))) for n in range(1, 9)]\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.start()\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.join()\n    assert sorted(g[\"pgid\"] for g in jobs.read_record(path)[\"groups\"]) == list(range(1, 9))\n",

          "end_line": 5664,
          "excerpt": "def replace_record(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write the record whole or not at all: a temporary file in its directory, then an atomic rename\n    (`Path.replace`, which is `os.replace`).\n\n    `Path.write_text` truncates first and writes after; a write that fails between the two keeps a\n    record cut short, and the record is the only copy of its rounds (DL-A-4 of the deep review). The\n    temporary file never outlives a failed write.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    handle, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=path.parent)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n            stream.write(text)\n            stream.flush()\n            # Reconciliation also replaces findings.md: retain its permissions instead of\n            # installing mkstemp's private mode. Fresh external records keep that private mode.\n            if path.exists():\n                os.fchmod(stream.fileno(), path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777)\n            os.fsync(stream.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

    "263092260c1ac0fda724743b2669b31affb56d4e": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-23T09:55:46Z",
      "body": "The third D-52 condition — every reader on one access point — was shown in\ne02c915. This commit takes the copy away:\n\n- .beads/issues.jsonl is no longer tracked, and is git-ignored so a\n  `git add -A` cannot bring it back. The export-identity gate and its four\n  tests are retired: there is no committed file left to compare.\n- The hosted CI hydrates the tracker, renders once and presets BEAD_RENDER;\n  every gate of the run reads that one render. Locally the access point\n  (scripts/bead_render.py) renders fresh through tools/bd, and without bd it\n  fails with both ways out — bootstrap or BEAD_RENDER — instead of reading a\n  stale copy.\n- The drift job hydrates too: plans-registry-strict reads the tracker, and\n  without the copy it would have crashed nightly. plans-registry and\n  plans-registry-strict declare needs_tracker; the schema now allows it in\n  both jobs.\n- The kit role geruest is dissolved: without the copy its remaining members\n  map to one export verdict, which the AK-6 test forbids. The stub files stay\n  with the export manifest. Two REIST_NICHT entries for tests that do not\n  travel were removed; the probe cap stays at 31.\n- verify_all.sh --ci measures the same gate set as the derived workflow\n  (finding 2 of the PR #32 review).\n- AGENTS.md house rules 2 and 4, README, plans/_README.md: the render is the\n  contract; a pull request body names every bead it opens, changes or closes\n  (maintainer, 2026-09-23, D-52 successor; the CI job summary follows as\n  bead coding-harness-1jg.4).\n- The empty gate-placement change package is archived (its bead 1jg.2 closed\n  with PR #32).\n\nStarted by a Cline session that stopped mid-way (uncommitted, last edit\n10:28); finished and corrected by Claude Code.\n\nVerified 2026-09-23: make verify VERIFY GREEN (325 passed, 15 skipped);\nverify_all.sh --job drift VERIFY GREEN, measuring the tracker locally.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "provenance.yaml"
      ]
    },
    "9446abe50f3a259d0ff515c3123ea5197f0f9293": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-20T23:42:48Z",
      "body": "decisions/gates.yaml declares what each gate measures, and thereby what reaches a\nmerge. It stood without a class while docs/governance/regelwerk.md beside it is\nhuman-decided; the commit guard of the review-swarm runner could only refuse it\nthrough a hard-coded list (R-22 of the review-swarm review).\n\nThe maintainer's answer in the night interview of 2026-10-20 (Q-1, option A): the\nsame class as the rulebook. Gate changes then always travel as a decision pull\nrequest.\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "9446abe50f3a259d0ff515c3123ea5197f0f9293",
      "subject": "decide(provenance): the gate definitions are human-decided",

    "a7ec2d696573b72ebeb56256dcd3241c223e2252": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T15:33:04Z",
      "body": "The maintainer answered \"yes\" to the ADR question of the change that\nbrought ADR answers into Coding Harness: it decides, among weighed\nalternatives, that the maintainer's merge of a pull request confirms a\ndecision instead of a signed commit. This records that decision as an ADR\nof its own, so it no longer lives only in a change folder that will be\narchived.\n\nThe ADR weighs four options: signed commits as in LakeSwitch, the merge\nwith an ask rule (chosen), a bot identity for agents, and documentation\nonly. Its consequences name the limits: a rule, not proof, since agents\nact under the maintainer's GitHub account; the bot identity as the upgrade\npath; LakeSwitch keeping its own signing until it switches; every pull\nrequest saying whether it decides.\n\nIt takes effect by its own merge. Its header says accepted, the state it\nhas on main, and leaves review empty, because no agent writes an approval\nfor a merge that has not happened.\n\nAGENTS.md house rule 8, docs/WORKFLOW.md and the signing how-to now point\nto it. It amends no interview decision, so the decision-continuity map\nneeds no entry; docs/adr/ has no index.\n\nmake verify: green.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "a7ec2d696573b72ebeb56256dcd3241c223e2252",
      "subject": "docs(adr): ADR 0008, the maintainer's merge confirms a decision",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [

        "docs/WORKFLOW.md",
        "docs/adr/0008-merge-confirms-a-decision.md"
      ]
    },

A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def write_atomic(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Replace ``path`` with ``data``: temporary file, fsync, rename, directory fsync; the mode is kept.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        mode = path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        path.write_bytes(data)  # nothing earlier to lose; the process umask applies as for any new file\n        return\n    handle, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=path.parent)\n    temporary = Path(name)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"wb\") as out:\n            out.write(data)\n            out.flush()\n            os.fsync(out.fileno())\n        temporary.chmod(mode)\n        temporary.replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n        raise\n    directory = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)\n    try:\n        os.fsync(directory)\n    finally:\n        os.close(directory)\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too.           "excerpt": "def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish `text` at `path` whole or not at all (same-directory temporary file, then rename).\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(text)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_records_are_schema_validated_and_atomic(state: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an invalid or partial record becomes visible, or concurrent updates overwrite each other\n    (criterion 19).\"\"\"\n    job_id = jobs.new_job_id()\n    path = record_path(job_id)\n    good = jobs.new_record(job_id, [\"echo\", \"hi\"], \"/work\", str(state / f\"{job_id}.log\"))\n    for broken in (\n        {**good, \"schema\": True},\n        {**good, \"schema\": 1.0},\n        {**good, \"state\": \"sleeping\"},\n        {**good, \"command\": []},\n        {**good, \"groups\": [{\"pgid\": \"x\", \"pid\": 1, \"start\": None}]},\n        {k: v for k, v in good.items() if k != \"log\"},\n        {**good, \"extra\": 1},\n    ):\n        with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n            jobs.write_record(path, broken)\n        assert not path.exists(), \"an invalid record was published\"\n    jobs.write_record(path, good)\n    before = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    real_fsync = os.fsync\n\n    def failing_fsync(_fd: int) -> None:\n        raise OSError(\"disk\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", failing_fsync)\n    with pytest.raises(OSError, match=\"disk\"):\n        jobs.write_record(path, {**good, \"state\": \"running\"})\n    monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"fsync\", real_fsync)\n    assert path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == before, \"a failed write left a partial record\"\n    assert sorted(p.name for p in state.iterdir()) == [path.name]  # no temporary file remains\n    path.write_text(before[: len(before) // 2], encoding=\"utf-8\")  # a truncated record is refused, never repaired\n    with pytest.raises(jobs.JobError):\n        jobs.read_record(path)\n    path.write_text(before, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    def add(n: int):\n        return lambda record: record[\"groups\"].append({\"pgid\": n, \"pid\": n, \"start\": None})\n\n    threads = [threading.Thread(target=jobs.update_record, args=(path, add(n))) for n in range(1, 9)]\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.start()\n    for thread in threads:\n        thread.join()\n    assert sorted(g[\"pgid\"] for g in jobs.read_record(path)[\"groups\"]) == list(range(1, 9))\n",

          "excerpt": "def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish `text` at `path` whole or not at all (same-directory temporary file, then rename).\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(text)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "def replace_record(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write the record whole or not at all: a temporary file in its directory, then an atomic rename\n    (`Path.replace`, which is `os.replace`).\n\n    `Path.write_text` truncates first and writes after; a write that fails between the two keeps a\n    record cut short, and the record is the only copy of its rounds (DL-A-4 of the deep review). The\n    temporary file never outlives a failed write.\n    \"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    handle, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=path.parent)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as stream:\n            stream.write(text)\n            stream.flush()\n            # Reconciliation also replaces findings.md: retain its permissions instead of\n            # installing mkstemp's private mode. Fresh external records keep that private mode.\n            if path.exists():\n                os.fchmod(stream.fileno(), path.stat().st_mode & 0o7777)\n            os.fsync(stream.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "def publish_atomic(plan: Path, content: bytes) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Replace `plan` with `content`: temporary file, fsync, rename, directory fsync; the mode is kept.\n\n    The destination must already exist; a missing plan is never recreated.\n    Failures before replacement leave the plan unchanged and remove the temporary\n    file. After replacement, a directory failure raises `PublishedButNotSynced`:\n    the record is already written and callers must not report it as unwritten.\n    \"\"\"\n    mode = plan.stat().st_mode & 0o7777\n    handle, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f\".{plan.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=plan.parent)\n    temporary = Path(name)\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"wb\") as out:\n            out.write(content)\n            out.flush()\n            os.fsync(out.fileno())\n        temporary.chmod(mode)\n        temporary.replace(plan)\n    except BaseException:\n        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n        raise\n    try:\n        directory = os.open(plan.parent, os.O_RDONLY)\n        try:\n            os.fsync(directory)\n        finally:\n            os.close(directory)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise PublishedButNotSynced(error.strerror or str(error)) from error\n",

          "excerpt": "def holding_key(key: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"One runner per loop record at a time (R-14 of the review-swarm review), by the record's key.\n\n    Two runners that both read `consumed: []` pay the same members and number the same round twice,\n    and the doubled ids then block `repair`. The lock is advisory, held by the open descriptor, and\n    a descriptor dies with its process - so a crashed run leaves no lock behind to break the next.\n    Supersession holds its own and every selected worktree's lock in one deterministic order, so it\n    cannot bypass a normal user of either record (bead coding-harness-e82i, criterion 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    path = record_base() / f\"{key}.lock\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"a+\") as handle:\n        try:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)\n        except BlockingIOError as error:\n            raise Refused(f\"another run holds the loop record `{key}`; one runner at a time\") from error\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "def receipt_lock(path: Path):\n    \"\"\"Serialize receipt publication and the final identity check/removal across processes.\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    descriptor = os.open(path.with_suffix(\".lock\"), os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)\n    with os.fdopen(descriptor, \"a\") as handle:\n        fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n",

          "excerpt": "class Store:\n    \"\"\"One change's research state directory.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, directory, *, scrub: Callable[[str], str] | None = None):\n        self.directory = Path(directory)\n        self._scrub = scrub\n        self._lock_fd = None\n\n    # -- placement --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def assert_outside(self, *forbidden, home=None):\n        \"\"\"Refuse a store inside (or equal to) any directory a model, the worktree or git may see.\n\n        ``home`` is the real home directory Claude research processes inherit; a store beneath it is refused\n        with the way out (Q-15): ``XDG_STATE_HOME`` must point outside it.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Resolve ``..`` and parent links before comparing (F-19): a lexical spelling must not slip past.\n        mine = Path(os.path.realpath(self.directory))\n        if home is not None:\n            base = Path(os.path.realpath(home))\n            if mine == base or mine.is_relative_to(base) or base.is_relative_to(mine):\n                raise StoreWriteError(\n                    f\"the state store would lie inside the home directory {base}, which Claude research \"\n                    \"processes inherit; set XDG_STATE_HOME to a directory outside it\"\n                )\n        for other in forbidden:\n            other = Path(os.path.realpath(other))\n            if mine == other or mine.is_relative_to(other) or other.is_relative_to(mine):\n                raise StoreWriteError(f\"the state store must stay outside {other}\")\n\n    def _ensure(self):\n        \"\"\"Create the owner-only directory, or refuse a link, a foreign owner or loose modes.\"\"\"\n        try:\n            self.directory.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            with contextlib.suppress(FileExistsError):\n                self.directory.mkdir(mode=0o700)\n            info = self.directory.lstat()\n        except OSError as error:\n            raise StoreWriteError(f\"cannot create the state store: {error}\") from error\n        if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != os.getuid() or stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) & 0o077:\n            raise StoreWriteError(\"the state store is a link, not ours or not owner-only\")\n\n    # -- the lock ---------",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_entry(line: str) -> Record | None:\n    \"\"\"One fixed-format record from one line, or None - the shared grammar of writer and report.\n\n    A leading \"- \" bullet is not part of the record. A line without the exact\n    form - the stamped span, the explicit seconds, the metadata and the marker\n    - stays unread; prose never becomes a duration here.\n    \"\"\"\n    body = line[2:].strip() if line.startswith(\"- \") else line\n    matched = RECORD.fullmatch(body)\n    if matched is None:\n        return None\n    return Record(\n        seconds=int(matched.group(\"seconds\")),\n        verb=matched.group(\"verb\").strip(),\n        attempt=int(matched.group(\"attempt\")),\n        route=matched.group(\"route\").strip(),\n        model=matched.group(\"model\").strip(),\n        result=matched.group(\"result\"),\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_time_line(content: str) -> TimeRecord | None:\n    \"\"\"One fixed-format record, or None; only its explicit seconds count (the shared parser).\"\"\"\n    parsed = time_records.parse_entry(content)\n    if parsed is None:\n        return None\n    return TimeRecord(\n        seconds=parsed.seconds,\n        verb=parsed.verb,\n        attempt=parsed.attempt,\n        route=parsed.route,\n        model=parsed.model,\n        result=parsed.result,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_shared_format_preserves_runner_bytes_and_midnight() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 2. Planted fault: changed metadata, a different suffix, or a midnight span without its end date.\"\"\"\n    end = START + dt.timedelta(seconds=600)\n    same_day = time_records.format_entry(START, end, 600, \"implement\", 1, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"accepted\")\n    assert same_day == (\n        \"2026-10-20 10:00:00–10:10:00 UTC, 600 s — implement · attempt 1 · route flash · \"\n        \"model glm-5.3-flash · accepted · measured by the runner\"\n    )\n    # The named outcome is the only difference between the two verdicts' lines.\n    rejected = time_records.format_entry(START, end, 600, \"implement\", 1, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"rejected\")\n    assert rejected == same_day.replace(\"accepted\", \"rejected\")\n    # A span across midnight carries the end's date; a same-day span carries none.\n    midnight_start = dt.datetime(2026, 10, 20, 23, 59, 30, tzinfo=dt.UTC)\n    midnight_end = dt.datetime(2026, 10, 21, 0, 0, 16, tzinfo=dt.UTC)\n    across = time_records.format_entry(\n        midnight_start, midnight_end, 45, \"implement\", 2, \"flash\", \"glm-5.3-flash\", \"rejected\"\n    )\n    assert across == (\n        \"2026-10-20 23:59:30–2026-10-21 00:00:16 UTC, 45 s — implement · attempt 2 · route flash · \"\n        \"model glm-5.3-flash · rejected · measured by the runner\"\n    )\n    # The fixed line survives the shared parser with every field intact, and prose stays unread.\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(across) == time_records.Record(\n        seconds=45, verb=\"implement\", attempt=2, route=\"flash\", model=\"glm-5.3-flash\", result=\"rejected\"\n    )\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(same_day + \" (approx)\") is None\n    assert time_records.parse_entry(\"2026-10-20 10:00–10:10 UTC, 600 s\") is None\n",

          "excerpt": "def research_dir(change, root):\n    \"\"\"``record_dir(change, root)/research`` without importing the runner (same XDG rule, read at call time).\n\n    The key is the runner's own record key - the change and a digest of the resolved repository root -\n    so two worktrees of the same change keep two research directories (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    state = os.environ.get(\"XDG_STATE_HOME\")\n    base = Path(state) if state else Path.home() / \".local\" / \"state\"\n    key = f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(Path(root).resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n    return base / \"coding-harness\" / \"stage2\" / key / \"research\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def _atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish `text` at `path` whole or not at all (same-directory temporary file, then rename).\"\"\"\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)\n    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f\".{path.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\")\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(text)\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        Path(temporary).replace(path)\n    except BaseException:\n        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n            Path(temporary).unlink()\n        raise\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "### The review loop (phase 4b)\n\n**Fresh availability-enabled runs (Q-16, ADR 0021):** first run\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py prepare-loop <change>`. The runner refreshes Pi's\ncatalog and probes admitted candidates with static input and no tools.\nTimed exclusions are skipped without a call; GLM through OpenCode Go is not\nexcluded (the 2026-10-21 GLM outage covers the Z.ai route only). Paid candidates require known cost, admitted terms and catalog presence.\nReport its timestamped reachable/failed/skipped list and selected stages in\nthe main Claude Code or Codex conversation, then invoke `review-loop <change>\n--availability-reported <id>` with the printed report id. This acknowledges\nthe report; the runner cannot inspect the conversation UI. The external\nreceipt is bound to the worktree, configuration and diff and expires after\n900 seconds. Changed inputs or failed preparation invalidate it. Preparation\nadds one actual call per tested candidate and is no review-quality or billing\nmeasurement. Up to three cheapest reachable paid candidates dynamically fill\nthe Flash swarm; the remaining reachable paid candidates form the ladder.\nExisting snapshots and legacy declarations without the rule retain the\nbehavior below. A run with history cannot be reset by preparation.\n\n**Paid terms expire (ADR 0022, bead coding-harness-abra).** Every\n`modelle_terms` record of a paid model carries `valid_until`, a quoted ISO\ncalendar date the reading is valid through; the following UTC day it is\nexpired, and the judgement reads UTC, never the local calendar. A record\nwithout a usable `valid_until` — missing, not a quoted date, or an impossible\ncalendar date — grants no admission, and the runner never infers, extends or\nrenews a date at runtime. A refusal names the model, says whether the expiry\nis missing, invalid or passed, and names the recorded date once it has\npassed. From seven UTC days before expiry through the expiry day,\npreparation and every round — fresh, legacy or resumed — print a warning\nwith the model id and date, and the round's notes carry it, so the released\nfindings keep it; a warning neither admits nor refuses, an expired reading\nis a skip with its reason, not a warning, and a skipped record with a valid\ndate warns too. A saved selection or a fresh receipt does not keep an\nexpired member admissible: the round is refused before the call, and the\nrun's history stands. Renewal is not the runner's: a reading is introduced\nor renewed by an agent's dated source re-read and a decision pull request\nmerged by the maintainer; where the source states an end date it is\nrecorded, and otherwise a record expires `gelesen` plus 30 calendar days.\nMigrated 2026-10-26 on that rule; both DeepSeek readings carry the\ndocumented 2026-10-25 source re-read and expire 2026-10-31.\n\nAfter implementation and before phase 6, `review-loop` runs one round per\ncall, and the loop runs **until a round is clean — every row of a round\ndecided and none accepted (ADR 0021).** Round 1 is the **free swarm**: a\nforced live catalog refresh (`pi update --models` before `pi --list-models`,\nno stale cache listed) discovers the models the `opencode-go` provider offers,\nand the `free_stage` rule in `model-endpoints.yaml` — provider, id suffix,\nincludes, excludes — selects the members; they review in parallel, each with\nno tools, from a scratch directory, and their only input is the\nimplementation diff: bounded hunks of source and test code against the merge\nbase with `origin/main`, uncommitted and untracked code included. The catalog\nis a live intermediary (`pi.dev`): the check proves which catalog was read,\nnot what OpenCode Go bills. The prompt carries the implementation diff up to\nthe shared bound of `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (4000 lines); a cut, whether by\nthat bound or by the free stage's own file or total limits, is recorded in the\nround, and a round over a cut diff never counts as clean (R-12, R-15). When\nevery free member fails with a rate-limit (429) or unavailability error, ",

          "excerpt": "def read_state(record: str | None, findings_text: str) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's stage snapshot: the record's own line first, else the last release's.\n\n    Only the runner's own lines are read - the released block is cut at\n    `Kept from the loop record:`, so the reviewers' words are never a snapshot\n    (criterion 13). A record without its state line predates the swarms and is\n    refused instead of continued with invented stages.\n    \"\"\"\n    line: str | None = None\n    if record is not None:\n        for text, reviewer in _record_lines(record):\n            if reviewer:\n                continue\n            match = STATE_LINE.match(text)\n            if match:\n                line = match.group(1)\n                break\n        if line is None:\n            raise Refused(\"the loop record has no Loop state line; it predates the swarms and cannot be continued.\")\n    else:\n        start = _last_release(findings_text)\n        if start >= 0:\n            block = findings_text[start:]\n            cut = KEPT_FROM.search(block)\n            if cut:\n                block = block[: cut.start()]\n            match = STATE_LINE.search(block)\n            if match is None:\n                # Every release of a record carries the snapshot; a block without it is not the runner's,\n                # and reading it as no run would let it end the loop (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n                raise Refused(\n                    \"the last released block in findings.md carries no Loop state line; the runner writes \"\n                    \"one with every release, so the block is not the runner's and the loop is not continued.\"\n                )\n            line = match.group(1)\n    if line is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        state = json.loads(line)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the run's Loop state line is not readable JSON: {error}\") from None\n    if (\n        not isinstance(state, dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"free\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"paid\"), dict)\n        or not isinstance(state.get(\"consumed\"), list)\n    ):\n        raise Refused(\"the run's Loop state line does not hold the expected stage snapshot.\")\n    return state\n",
